answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by tying influence to staked reputation that decays with inactivity: each agent locks a deposit, and its voting weight grows only through a long history of verified work, so a fresh identity starts in the umber shadow of zero trust. Cheap copies cannot wander in and outvote incumbents, because creating many identities multiplies the stake cost while splitting reputation. An inlet for newcomers stays open, anyone may join and earn weight slowly, but sudden bursts of identical new agents are quarantined for peer review before their votes count.
